document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 000746, "Policy on Track, But Violence Will Rise"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Neumann warns violence will rise and suicide bombing will be used for propaganda. He attributes the stronger insurgency to four years of Taliban reorganization in a sanctuary in Pakistan's tribal areas, which if unaddressed could revive the strategic threat that prompted OEF.

key_claims: Neumann expects violence to rise over the next several months, aimed at ISAF, Coalition forces and pro-government officials, with more suicide bombings in Kabul and other cities.
The shift to IEDs and suicide bombs is attributed to the failure of the Taliban's large-unit engagement tactics in early 2005.
Counternarcotics operations in Helmand will raise incident levels as the Taliban is forced to defend high-threat areas.
The Taliban's long-term strategy depends on keeping the Afghan government weak in the provinces.
The insurgency will continue as long as the Taliban can resupply from sanctuary beyond the reach of both governments.
Pakistani pressure on the Taliban is increasing, and the Tripartite process is building military links, but concerns about Pakistani capabilities remain.
The cable argues that rising violence does not indicate a failing policy.
